items.title: CCJ joins the $$$ Shopping List
items.summary: Buyer of 10,500 Dec $85 calls at $1.74 plus 5,000 Dec $75 calls at $4.75; spot $75.37. Uranium name, down ~18% YTD; desk sees the 200-week EMA as a bottom after the November low near $66.

items.title: BURL ($$): June 2027 $230 puts sold
items.summary: June 2027 $230 puts sold; spot ~$257. Off-price apparel retailer, down ~11% YTD after a July 52-week high near $378, with the September low near $227. Desk lean is the June 2027 $230 put sale.

items.title: CBRE joins the $$$ Shopping List
items.summary: December $135 calls bought; spot ~$138. Commercial real estate services name, down ~14% YTD after a February 52-week high near $174, with the October low near $121. Desk wants the December $135 calls.

items.title: Desk market wrap 11/9
items.summary: Stocks bounced to start the week as oil dropped another 3% and eased inflation fears, though AI financing stayed an overhang. SPY and QQQ squeezed back to the 8-day average on a wide-range session; desk waits on this week's inflation data. A few large call books adjusted.

items.title: Desk open wrap 11/9
items.summary: Futures firmer to start the week as oil kept falling and metals bid; VIX dropped again. Europe recovered some of last week's losses and Nikkei bounced after last week's slide. CPI is next.

items.title: ARES ($$): Mar 2027 $110 puts sold
items.summary: 600 March 2027 $110 puts sold at $6.58 on 10/28, still in open interest, after 1,250 December $115 ITM short puts opened 10/14 (~$1.2M); spot $134. Shares are down 17% YTD, bounced off the 10/15 low and reclaimed the 50- and 200-day on 10/29. Desk lean is selling puts on pullbacks toward the moving averages.

items.title: MSI ($$): Jan $560 calls bought
items.summary: 1,000 January $560 calls bought at $13 (~$1.3M) on 11/5, rolling up from 2,050 January $500 calls (~$4.25M) bought 11/4 into the report; spot ~$514.50. +34% YTD, spiked to a 52-week high then faded; $548 resistance, 21-day EMA near $483 first support. Desk wants adds on pullbacks toward the 21-day.

items.title: LH joins the $$$ Shopping List
items.summary: 400 May $410 calls, 300 May $350 calls, and 600 May $420 calls bought to open in late October (~$2.3M); spot ~$367. Diagnostics name +46% YTD, forming a post-earnings bull flag after a weekly flag that measures toward ~$420; desk wants the flag while it holds.

items.title: Desk market wrap 11/6
items.summary: Jobs print came in stronger and the dollar firmed; the AI complex faded after the open. NYAD stays in a sell signal, VIX held over 20, and SPY is trying to hold the rising 200-day into next week's inflation prints. Size put sellers were active in first-quarter 2027 in beaten-up quality names.

items.title: Desk open wrap 11/6
items.summary: Futures steadied after Thursday's plunge with jobs in focus; VIX still elevated after the spike. Tech led an early snapback while Europe and Asia sold off on AI-spend and valuation worries.

items.title: SBUX joins the $$$ Shopping List
items.summary: 7,500 January $105 calls remain in open interest from 7/31, with 2,000 January 2028 $95 short puts and 1,500 September $85 / $95 short puts opening; spot ~$107. Global coffeehouse turnaround (+26% YTD) probing $108–$110 resistance toward early-2025 $116 highs; desk watches strength through $110–$112 with comps, Rewards scale, and the $2B savings program as the hold.

items.title: PYPL ($$): Apr 2027 $67.50 calls bought
items.summary: 1,200 April 2027 $67.50 calls bought at $2.14 (~$256K) on 11/5, 500 January 2029 $55 ITM calls bought 10/30 (937 in OI), and 3,100 April 2027 $47.50 short puts still open from 9/14; spot $59. Desk sees a cheap payments turnaround holding the 200-day; lean is following long-dated call buyers on pullbacks toward the 50-day.

items.title: CBOE ($$): Dec $360 calls bought
items.summary: 325 December $360 calls bought at $16 (~$520K) on 11/5 into a 60-day high, after 350 December $340 calls (~$595K) on 10/30 and 750 June 2028 $400 calls (~$3M+) on 10/22; spot ~$353. Desk sees a +40% YTD exchange compounder pressing May highs with KPI event-contract launch ahead; add on pullbacks toward the short-term averages.

items.title: EPD joins the $$$ Shopping List
items.summary: 10,000 March $40 calls bought (~$980K) on 11/3, ~9,000 Dec $42 and ~9,000 Jan $42 long-call open interest, plus further accumulation in Jan 2027/2028 call strikes; spot $36.50. Desk watches a breakout over ~$39 toward ~$45 in an integrated midstream gas/NGL name that broke under a rising 200-day this week but still holds a longer-term weekly bull flag (+14% YTD).

items.title: TSCO ($$): Nov 13 $37.5 calls bought
items.summary: 6,000 Nov 13 (weekly) $37.5 calls bought on 11/4, rolling up from the $35s, as shares gapped to a 60-day high, 5,000 Nov $34 calls bought 10/19 (stock replacement), and 3,500 Nov $33.5 short puts opened; spot $36.60. Desk sees a rural retail / pet consumables name, down ~27% YTD and below the 200-day since February, but holding above the 8/21-day EMAs and 50-day with a bullish MACD cross. Desk watches a close through the 200-day as the trigger; traffic and pet comps improving.

items.title: UBER ($$): Jan 2029 $80 puts sold
items.summary: 900 Jan 2029 $80 ITM puts sold (~$1.5M) on 11/4 after Q3, 2,750 Jan $52.5 ITM calls bought (~$4M) into earnings 11/3, and large Dec $55 and $57.5 short-put open interest from late October; spot $69.90. Desk sees a mobility + delivery leader, down ~15% YTD; reclaimed the 21-day EMA on 2x volume after Q3, basing off the late-October low with the 50-day as first resistance. Cheap vs its own 10-year FCF range; desk lean is following long-dated put sellers on pullbacks.

items.title: MPWR joins the $$$ Shopping List
items.summary: 150 Feb $1400 calls bought (~$2.35M) on 11/3, rolling out of Nov $1200 calls, and 100 May $1300 short puts opened 8/11 in a strangle with $2260 calls; spot $1,328.30. Desk watches a breakout over ~$1400 in an AI-server power-management semi that has pulled back ~30% into a falling-wedge base holding anchored VWAP from the March lows.

items.title: VZ ($$): Jan 2029 $38 puts sold
items.summary: 1,000 Jan 2029 $38 puts sold at $3.88 (~$388K) on 11/2, 10,000 Dec $44 short puts opened 10/23, and 5,000 June 2027 $47 calls bought 10/13; spot $45.24. Desk sees a high-yield telecom at a cheap free-cash-flow multiple, below the converged 50- and 200-day near $47, with a break through that targeting the ~$51.70 September high.

items.title: INSM joins the $$$ Shopping List
items.summary: 5,000 Jan $110 calls bought at $8.62 on 11/3, 10,000 Jan $100/$130 call spreads bought 10/27, and 1,000 Jan $95 short puts opened 10/14; spot $104.44. Desk sees a respiratory biotech with a bronchiectasis drug at a blockbuster run-rate, holding above the 8- and 21-day EMAs, with ~$112 as resistance and the ~$93 October low as support.

items.title: Oil's war premium cracks
items.summary: Brent fell 11.4% Monday, its biggest daily drop in six months, after Iran signaled a return to talks. The open question is how much of oil was pricing real supply loss versus insurance, and a gap remains between negotiations and restored Gulf flows.

items.title: BofA: the data-center power squeeze and the elections
items.summary: BofA's utilities team sees state regulators and power-bill affordability, not which party wins, as the bigger election risk for the AI electricity buildout. Texas is the center of demand but its regulatory timetable matters most; Georgia and Ohio show how affordability politics reshape data-center economics.

items.title: Goldman: risk appetite breaks, leverage doesn't
items.summary: October saw one of the largest monthly drops in Goldman's risk appetite gauge in two decades, the sharpest deterioration since November 2021, but not yet at contrarian extremes. Hedge funds cut directional exposure while keeping gross leverage elevated, and the stock-vol-yields relationship is shifting, widening outcomes both ways.

items.title: Goldman: one more crowded long to clear
items.summary: Tech-focused hedge funds lost nearly 12% in October and managers are protecting year-end P&L rather than rebuilding risk. The net-exposure bounce is mostly short covering with gross leverage still very high; semis and AI infrastructure were liquidated while Mag 7 positioning sits near the year's highs and could become a source of funds.

items.title: UBS joins the $$$ Shopping List
items.summary: 2,700 Jan 2028 $52.5 calls bought (~$1.37M) on 10/1, still in open interest, and 1,450 Jan 2028 $60 straddles bought 9/9; spot about $48.45 near the 200-day and year-to-date VWAP. Desk sees a durable 2027 earnings story as merger integration costs roll off, with the Swiss capital rule as the main overhang.

items.title: WFC ($$): Nov $88 calls bought
items.summary: 1,650 Nov $88 calls bought at $0.71 on 11/2, 3,000 June $90 calls bought 9/22 at $6.10 still open, and 1,800 Jan 2028 $70 short puts building in open interest; spot about $85.90 after reclaiming the 50- and 200-day. Desk prefers short puts near $78 support; a break over ~$92 opens ~$98.

items.title: W ($$): June 2027 $105/$85 bull put spreads
items.summary: 2,500 June 2027 $105/$85 bull put spreads opened near $8 credit on 10/28 and 2,500 Jan $115 calls bought 9/29; spot about $113.10 just off a new high, earnings 11/4. Desk likes June bull put spreads near the 50-day (~$105).

items.title: Goldman: midterms and the policy risks markets may misprice
items.summary: A Democratic House looks increasingly likely but the Senate is less certain than prediction markets imply. Winning seats is not the same as changing policy; bigger fiscal fights likely come in 2027, data-center limits are more likely at state level, and effective tariff rates are expected to rise after the vote.

items.title: Goldman: seven signs from the hedge fund book
items.summary: Hedge-fund net leverage is near levels that historically preceded 20%+ drawdowns while the S&P sits only modestly off the highs. Implied correlation is near the lows, defensives look expensive, and systematic selling is a near-term obstacle.

items.title: Morgan Stanley: hedge funds go underweight AI
items.summary: Hedge funds are underweight AI for the first time since early 2023, the most sustained gross reduction in the prime-book history. Single-stock vol versus the index is at a record and pairwise correlation is under 10%, which may be a final clearing phase.

items.title: Goldman: spec gold futures selling
items.summary: About $19.5B of speculative gold futures were sold over five weeks, about $8B of that from Oct 20–27, mostly smaller reportable and non-reportable traders. About $3,850 is flagged as support.

items.title: BofA: turning constructive on US tech IG bonds
items.summary: Tech investment-grade bonds are at their worst relative underperformance in about 30 years. AI issuers have raised about $182B in bonds and $89B in equity in 2026, and the next big risk-on window is seen in the first half of 2027.

items.title: Bloomberg: equal-weight beat cap-weight by the most since 2009
items.summary: October's equal-weight minus cap-weight S&P gap was the widest since April 2009, while the Nasdaq 100 sat about 9% off its peak.
